game_mammals: Deer and antelope (pronghorn) killed by a motor vehicle on a public highway may be possessed only after notifying a conservation officer and receiving free written authorization (verbal OK for immediate possession, written authorization to follow). Statute does not cover elk, bighorn sheep, mountain goat, bison or other big game; those would need case-by-case officer handling.
game_birds: No roadkill provision for game birds (pheasant, turkey, grouse, etc.); the statute covers only deer and antelope, so possessing road-killed game birds is not authorized by it. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves, cranes) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Contact a local GFP conservation officer, who may issue a dated written authorization (no fee). The authorization must stay with the carcass during processing and storage.
timing: Must contact the officer before taking possession. A person who euthanizes a seriously injured animal must report it to GFP within 24 hours.
excluded_species: Anything other than deer and antelope is not covered (elk, bighorn sheep, mountain goat, bison, game birds, furbearers, protected and endangered species).
sale_of_parts: Prohibited. No part may be sold, bartered or traded.
other_restrictions: SD law separately allows a person to humanely euthanize a seriously injured animal, with a report to GFP within 24 hours. CWD rules: if deer or elk carcass parts leave the county of origin, remains must go to a waste-management provider or permitted landfill. No dumping in road ditches or on public land.
statute_or_reg: SDCL 41-1-5.7 (deer and antelope killed by motor vehicle)
agency: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks (GFP)
notes: Statute dates from 1992 (SL 1992, ch 294). The GFP FAQ confirms the officer-authorization process. The citation comes from a secondary source (animallaw.info) and matches the GFP FAQ wording.

game_mammals: Deer: any person may possess a deer accidentally killed by a motor vehicle for personal use and consumption, provided TWRA or a local law-enforcement agency is notified (name and address) within a reasonable time, not over 48 hours. Black bear: possession only if a TWRA enforcement officer authorizes it and issues a kill tag or receipt. The statute lets any person keep 'a wild animal' killed by a motor vehicle for personal use, subject to these conditions. Elk is not specifically addressed.
game_birds: Wild turkey: TWRA guidance (via a 2022 news report) says to notify TWRA or law enforcement within 48 hours, the same as deer. The statute's general allowance ('a wild animal killed by motor vehicle') seems to cover other resident game birds. Migratory birds and other federally protected birds are excluded by the statute and by the MBTA.
permit_process: Deer and turkey: notify TWRA or local law enforcement (a phone call is sufficient), giving name and address. Bear: a TWRA officer must authorize and issue a kill tag before possession.
timing: Within 48 hours for deer (and turkey per TWRA guidance). Bear: before possession. No seasonal limits.
excluded_species: Federally protected wildlife and species protected under T.C.A. Title 70 Chapter 8 (state endangered, threatened and nongame protected species), including raptors and migratory birds. Bear only with an officer-issued tag.
sale_of_parts: Personal use only. The statute says 'for personal use', so sale is not authorized.
other_restrictions: Motorists are not required to report game they hit. Violations are a Class C misdemeanor. Normal CWD carcass-transport rules apply, including restrictions on moving carcasses out of CWD Management Units.
notes: The TWRA FAQ confirms deer may be possessed with notification within 48 hours. The turkey 48-hour rule comes from a TWRA spokesperson in 2022 news coverage, not the statute text. Elk (a restored herd in East TN) is not specifically addressed, so contact TWRA.

game_mammals: Not allowed. TPWD treats an animal killed by a vehicle as taken by illegal means and methods, so it is illegal to possess. A dead deer may be moved off the roadway and left there; TxDOT or the county removes carcasses.
game_birds: Not allowed (same prohibition). Migratory birds are also federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: None. No salvage permit exists. Report injured deer to a TPWD game warden dispatcher.
excluded_species: All wildlife. Since a 2007 change, even nongame road-surface collection is not allowed.
other_restrictions: A person may move a deer they are sure is dead off the road but may not keep it. Injured animals: contact a game warden.
statute_or_reg: General Texas Parks & Wildlife Code possession prohibitions (illegal means and methods). A 2007 change tied to HB 12 (80th Legislature) removed the prior nongame roadkill allowance. No single roadkill-specific section was confirmed.
notes: The prohibition is well established (TPWD PIO statement to KXAN, March 2023). The exact code or TAC section was not confirmed, so the citation is low confidence.

game_mammals: No general public roadkill salvage permit program was found in Utah rules or the 2026 Big Game Field Regulations. Big game (deer, elk, moose, pronghorn, etc.) is protected wildlife and may not be possessed without a DWR-issued license, permit, tag, donation slip or certificate. Secondary sources say a person must contact DWR before taking a vehicle-killed deer or elk, and DWR may authorize possession, for example with a donation slip.
game_birds: No specific roadkill provision found. Protected game birds (turkey, upland) would need DWR authorization. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Contact DWR (regional office or conservation officer) before removing the animal. Possession may be authorized at officer discretion, for example by donation slip or certificate of registration. Report roadkill locations with the Utah Roadkill Reporter app (reporting only, not a salvage permit).
timing: Before possession. No statutory deadline found.
excluded_species: Unclear. Antlers or horns attached to a skull plate may not be possessed without DWR authorization; use the Deadhead Reporter. Endangered and threatened species and raptors are not salvageable.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized. Sale of big game parts is restricted under R657-5-20.
other_restrictions: CWD carcass importation and transport rules apply (R657-5-43, R657-5-18).
statute_or_reg: No roadkill-specific rule confirmed. General possession rules: Utah Code Title 23A (Wildlife Resources Act) and Utah Admin. Code R657-5 (big game) and R657-3 (possession of protected wildlife).
notes: Official DWR pages did not describe a roadkill salvage program, and the 2026 field regs contain no 'salvage' or 'roadkill' text. Secondary sources conflict (some say legal with DWR contact; LegalClarity says a 'certificate of registration' is required). Verify with DWR.

game_mammals: Deer, moose and bear killed by vehicles are handled by game wardens. The warden confirms a vehicle kill and may release the animal to a person (usually offered first to the driver, otherwise to a food shelf or a person on the warden's list) with a warden-issued tag or authorization number. Authorization is required before removal.
game_birds: No specific roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds. Possession of game without a license or authorization is generally prohibited, so contact a warden. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Call 911 or state police dispatch, which contacts the game warden. The warden issues a tag (a unique 5-digit number) before the animal is removed.
timing: Must obtain warden authorization before removal.
excluded_species: Not formally listed. Endangered and threatened species and protected birds are excluded. Furbearers and other species need warden authorization (secondary sources say a possession tag is needed for big game and furbearers).
sale_of_parts: Not authorized. Sale of big game meat is generally prohibited.
other_restrictions: Only wardens or listed officials may kill a deer injured beyond recovery (10 V.S.A. § 4749), with disposal under § 4513. Wardens collect teeth from bear and moose for biological data. Transporting roadkill across state lines is reportedly illegal. Vermonters only, per a 2015 news report.
statute_or_reg: 10 V.S.A. § 4749 (injured deer killing, disposal under § 4513). No roadkill-specific possession statute confirmed.
notes: The process is warden-driven and documented mainly by news reports (Seven Days 2015, The Bridge 2019) rather than a formal salvage rule. The exact regulatory basis for the warden tag was not confirmed.

game_mammals: A driver who strikes, or any person who finds, a deer, bear or elk killed in a vehicle collision may claim it for personal use at any time of year, as if lawfully killed in season. The claimant must immediately report to a conservation police officer or other local law-enforcement officer, who inspects the animal and awards it with a call-for-service or report number. If the driver does not claim it, the officer may award it to another person.
game_birds: Wild turkey is covered on the same terms as deer, bear and elk. Other game birds are not covered. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Report to a conservation police officer (DWR) or local law enforcement. The officer inspects the animal and issues a call-for-service or report number.
excluded_species: Only deer, bear, turkey and elk are covered. All other species (furbearers, small game, nongame, protected and endangered species, raptors) are not authorized under this section.
sale_of_parts: For the claimant's own use. Sale is not authorized (general game-sale prohibitions apply).
other_restrictions: An animal injured badly enough to need euthanasia may be awarded after officer inspection. Virginia's CWD carcass-transport restrictions still apply, including moving carcasses out of Disease Management Areas.
statute_or_reg: Va. Code § 29.1-539 (Claiming deer, bear, turkey, or elk struck by motor vehicle)
notes: Amended by 2024 Acts c. 83, which broadened coverage. The section title now lists deer, bear, turkey and elk, and lets finders as well as drivers claim.

game_mammals: Deer and elk killed by motor vehicle collision only. A free WDFW salvage permit is required within 24 hours of taking possession. Columbian white-tailed deer may never be salvaged. In 2025 WDFW opened deer salvage in Clark, Cowlitz and Wahkiakum counties (previously closed to protect Columbian white-tailed deer); elk have been allowed since 2016. Moose, bear, bighorn sheep, mountain goat and cougar are not covered.
game_birds: Not covered. Only deer and elk may be salvaged. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Free printable Roadkill Salvage Permit through WDFW's online application, or at WDFW regional offices. Keep the signed, dated hardcopy with the meat until all edible parts are consumed. Big game hunting licenses and tags cannot be used.
timing: Permit within 24 hours of taking possession. Eastern Region (100-series GMUs): submit CWD samples (head with at least 3 inches of neck, or lymph nodes) within 5 days of receiving the permit.
excluded_species: All species except deer and elk. Columbian white-tailed deer are always excluded.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed on the WDFW page. Sale of salvaged game is presumed not allowed under general wildlife-sale prohibitions (unverified).
other_restrictions: The entire carcass, including entrails, must be removed from the right-of-way. Only law enforcement or WDFW-authorized people may euthanize injured animals; the public may not kill an injured animal to salvage it. No trespassing. CWD transport limits apply (WAC 220-413-030), and carcasses may not cross WA/OR/ID/BC lines unless criteria are met. Unfit meat and parts go to disposal under WAC 246-203-121.
statute_or_reg: WAC 220-400-040 (Possession of dead wildlife; salvage provisions now in subsection (4)); RCW 77.15.750 (penalties); WAC 220-413-030 (CWD and carcass transport)
agency: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW)
notes: WSR 26-09-032 (effective May 8, 2026) renumbered the salvage text in WAC 220-400-040 and added shed-antler rules; salvage requirements are otherwise unchanged. In 2022 the Commission denied a petition to expand species and allow citizen dispatch.

game_mammals: Wildlife killed or mortally wounded by an accidental motor-vehicle strike may be possessed. This covers deer, bear (adult) and other game animals. Elk, spotted fawns and bear cubs are excluded.
game_birds: Game birds such as wild turkey and grouse appear to be covered by the general 'wildlife' language. 'Protected birds' are excluded, and migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Notify an appropriate law-enforcement agency, then obtain a free non-hunting game tag from WVDNR (Electronic Licensing / Check Game system or a DNR office). The tag must be attached to the carcass.
timing: Notify law enforcement within 12 hours of the incident. Obtain the non-hunting game tag within 24 hours of taking possession.
excluded_species: Elk, spotted fawns, bear cubs and protected birds (plus state and federal endangered species).
sale_of_parts: Not specified in the statute. Sale of wildlife is generally prohibited in WV, so presume no sale.
other_restrictions: The collision must be accidental or inadvertent. Statewide CWD carcass-transport rules apply (restrictions on moving carcasses out of CWD Containment Areas).
agency: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources (WVDNR)
notes: The statute directs the DNR director to set procedures. Online tagging of non-hunting game is through the WVDNR licensing and Check Game system; the exact current mechanics were not verified.

game_mammals: Deer: the driver has first priority. If the driver declines, another person at the scene may take it. Register with DNR (online or by phone at 608-267-7691) with a DNR customer ID before removing it from the scene; no tag or harvest authorization is needed after that. Bear: a tag or approval from a law-enforcement officer or DNR is required before removal, and the carcass must be tagged within 24 hours of receiving instructions. Elk is not covered by s. 29.349, so contact a conservation warden.
game_birds: Wild turkey: same as deer. Register with DNR before possessing or removing it from the scene; the driver has priority. Other small game, including upland birds: only during the open season and only if the person holds the required hunting or trapping license. Migratory birds are excluded and federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Deer and turkey: vehicle-killed registration online through DNR GoWild (gowild.wi.gov/wildlife/harvest/carkill) or by phone at 608-267-7691. Bear: call the DNR law-enforcement non-emergency line for a tag. Tags are free.
timing: Deer and turkey: register before removal from the scene. Bear: tag within 24 hours of receiving officer instructions. Small game: open season only.
excluded_species: Fisher, otter, bobcat, wolf, migratory birds, and protected, endangered and threatened species. Elk is not covered.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized. General prohibitions on sale of wild game apply.
other_restrictions: Deer must comply with CWD carcass-transport rules (NR 10). Small-game possession requires the appropriate license and an open season. Carcass removal from roadways is requested through the local Sheriff.
statute_or_reg: Wis. Stat. § 29.349 (Animals killed by motor vehicles); § 29.354 (possession exemption)
notes: Statute text was reviewed. Administrative details (NR 10 and NR 19) and elk handling were not verified.

game_mammals: Antelope (pronghorn), deer, elk, moose and wild bison killed in an unintentional vehicle collision may be collected after obtaining Game and Fish authorization. Other big game (bighorn sheep, mountain goat, black or grizzly bear, mountain lion) is not covered.
game_birds: Wild turkey is covered with authorization. Other upland birds (grouse, pheasant, partridge) are not covered. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Electronic authorization through the WGFD Roadkill Collection Application or the 'Report Roadkill' button in the Wyoming 511 app (requires a WGFD username). A certificate issues immediately after a short questionnaire and works without cell service. The rule also allows a permit, donation coupon or Interstate Game Tag.
timing: Authorization before taking possession. Collection only from sunrise to sunset.
excluded_species: All species except antelope, deer, elk, moose, wild bison and wild turkey (for example bighorn sheep, mountain goat, bears, mountain lion, wolves, furbearers and other game birds). Excluded locations: Interstates 25, 80 and 90, active construction and maintenance zones, and National Park Service roads.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed in Chapter 70. Wyoming generally prohibits sale of game meat, so presume no sale (unverified).
other_restrictions: Remove the entire animal (edible and inedible parts) from the right-of-way. No field dressing in the right-of-way. Park at least 2 feet off the roadway with flashers on. Present the animal for inspection on request. No entering private property without permission. The rule does not authorize euthanizing injured animals. CWD (deer, elk, moose): whole carcasses may not leave Wyoming; the head and spinal column must go to an approved landfill or incinerator unless taken to a CWD sampling site; only listed parts (boned meat, cleaned hide, cleaned skull or antlers, teeth, finished mounts) may be transported. False statements are a violation.
statute_or_reg: Wyoming Game and Fish Commission Regulation Chapter 70, Possession of Road Killed Wildlife (authority W.S. 23-3-106, 23-3-310)
notes: Adopted November 16, 2021, after 2021 legislation; electronic authorization launched in early 2022. WGFD reminders in November 2024 and November 2025 confirm the same species and rules.
